subject: Proposal: bridged commit + multipart uplift options
messages:
From: Evan Carter <evan.carter@aureliushealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@aureliushealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-18T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-cycle uplift + co-term options

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last month — the team liked the throughput numbers and the KV caching profile. We just finished a usage review and expect to exceed our committed monthly tokens by ~45% for Q3 due to a pilot that scaled faster than anticipated. Attached is our Q2 export for context (Aurelius_usage_Q2_2027.csv).

We need two things:
- Options to add capacity now (mid-contract uplift) that won't blow our forecasting.
- A way to co-term the uplift with our current annual contract so we aren't managing multiple renewal dates. Ideally we’d avoid a 12-month cliff for the additional units.

Quick constraints:
- Target effective discount on the incremental spend: 8–12% if we commit to a 6–9 month bridged path.
- Procurement needs paperwork by 8/26 to hit next billing cycle.

Can you share 2–3 structured options (pricing + billing cadence + co-term/annualize mechanics) and any timing implications for procurement? If you can include an option that uses a voucher/bridged-commit (we like the flexibility), that would be great.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Carter
Head of Platform Engineering, Aurelius Health
450 Park Ave, Suite 1200
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Carter <evan.carter@aureliushealth.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@aureliushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-18T19:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle uplift + co-term options

Hi Evan — appreciate the context and the usage dump. Attached is a short spreadsheet with three straightforward options (proposed-uplift-options.xlsx). Summary here so procurement can move quickly: 

Option A (Pro-rata uplift)
- Add 45% additional capacity immediately. Billed pro-rata on next invoice.
- One-time 10% discount on incremental units for the remainder of the contract term.
- Co-term: no change to original renewal date; uplift expires at current term end (no annualize).

Option B (Bridged commit + voucher) — recommended for flexibility
- Create a 6-month bridged commit equal to 70% of the observed Q3 excess usage as a voucher bucket.
- Voucher draws down against overage; voucher purchased up-front and billed pro-rata or via a short amendment.
- Effective discount range: 8–12% depending on upfront commit and payment term.
- Co-term: we can auto-annualize the unused portion at your next renewal with a blended rate, or let voucher simply roll off.

Option C (Annualize staircase)
- Immediate uplift with staged annualization: 33% now, 33% at 3 months, remainder at renewal.
- Discount tiers at commit thresholds (12% at >= 2x baseline increment).

Timing and approvals: procurement deadline 8/26 is tight but doable for Option B if we have finance alignment (billing path and PO). I’ve looped in Marissa and Aditya for pricing approval / payment term signoff.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Evan: flag which option you prefer (A/B/C) and whether finance wants an upfront voucher or monthly pro-rated charge.
2) If Option B: We’ll produce an amendment + voucher invoice and target sign by 8/25 to meet procurement.
3) Marissa/Aditya: can you confirm discount headroom for a voucher deal and whether we can do net-30 vs net-45 for this customer?

Thanks — I’ll hold a fast cadence if useful.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle uplift + co-term options

Quick internal:

Thanks, Mina — Option B is the preferred commercial construct (voucher/bridged). Approvals/constraints below:
- Pricing: we can go to 12% effective discount if customer signs for >= 6-month bridged voucher covering at least 60% of the observed Q3 overage AND agrees to auto-annualize any unused voucher capacity at renewal with a blended rate.
- Payment: finance will accept net-45 for the voucher if they provide a PO and commit to electronic payment (no exceptions). Net-30 otherwise.
- Legal: amendment language to explicitly describe voucher drawdown and co-term auto-annualize needs to be clear — avoid an open-ended carry-forward.

If that sits with you, Mina, we can draft an amendment and one-page SOW for procurement to attach to the PO. Evan’s 8/26 timeline is tight but achievable.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Operations
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Evan Carter <evan.carter@aureliushealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@aureliushealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-21T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle uplift + co-term options

Mina / team — thanks for the quick follow-up and the three options. We discussed internally and want to proceed with Option B (bridged commit / voucher). A few clarifications before procurement routes this: 

- We will purchase a 6-month voucher sized at 70% of our projected Q3 overage. Please size the invoice and include the blended discount (12% as discussed).
- Billing: we will take net-45 and will provide a PO by 8/24. Can you send the amendment + voucher invoice so Legal/Procurement can review?
- Co-term: please include the auto-annualize clause so any unused voucher at renewal converts to committed units at the blended rate. Our preferred renewal anchor for the annualized portion is January 31, 2028.

I’ve attached a signed term-sheet draft from our side (signed-term-sheet-draft.pdf) to speed approvals. If you can get the amendment & invoice by tomorrow (8/22), procurement will have time to approve and issue the PO on 8/24.

Best — Evan
Evan Carter
Head of Platform Engineering, Aurelius Health
